steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Heracles (Hercules in Roman) was the greatest Greek hero, son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hera hated Heracles because he was proof of Zeus's infidelity — she sent two snakes to kill him in his cradle

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Heracles was driven mad by Hera and killed his wife Megara and their children

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Twelve Labours were his punishment and path to redemption, set by King Eurystheus of Tiryns

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why did Hera hate Heracles? | Q: What was the purpose of the Twelve Labours? | Q: How does Heracles fit the pattern of the Greek hero?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Heracles was the son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene, making him living proof of Zeus's infidelity. Hera's hatred was motivated by jealousy and a desire to punish Zeus's illegitimate offspring. | They were Heracles' penance for killing his wife and children in a fit of Hera-induced madness. The oracle at Delphi instructed him to serve King Eurystheus for twelve years. | He has divine parentage (son of Zeus), shows extraordinary strength from childhood, performs impossible deeds (the Labours), suffers greatly (madness, servitude, death), and achieves immortality.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When discussing Heracles, always connect his story to the wider concept of the Greek hero Use specific Labours as evidence — don't just say 'he completed tasks' The theme of suffering is central to Heracles — examiners want to see this recognised Compare Heracles with other heroes if the question allows it Remember that Heracles' story has a moral dimension: great deeds come at great personal cost
